study.question: Does removing only one or two item coordinates preserve near-source click quality and reduce measured cost across native and source-coupled scratch initialization, or is the width14 observation dependent on initialization or hardware shape?
study.hypothesis: Observed limitation: broad reductions and reallocation have repeatedly lost click AUC. Source g2-r0004-context_only is 0.660646940486458 with 32,060,453 parameters. g1-r0016-coupled_item14_action16 is 0.660482133621223 (delta -0.000164806865235), 29,012,475 parameters (9.507% fewer), p50/p95 9.1347/9.1885ms versus contemporaneous full16 11.6831/11.9739ms, validation wall23.7838 versus24.7628s, and train268.1038 versus276.2208s. These are single-seed observations, not established retention or timing causation. Coupled item12 is 0.6581366143021284 and native item12 is 0.6583083293967678: coupling is not generally beneficial and capacity response is not monotonic. Mechanism hypothesis: close to full width, item representation and associated scorer/tower input capacity can be slightly reduced while maintaining useful signal; the putative useful region is 14-15, not the strongly compressed widths. Width15 is a prospective new dose; native14 and native15 separate the usefulness of the representation size from a favorable source-coordinate initialization. Width15 may have slower kernels than14 despite fewer operations; that would fail a speed claim for15. This is a local efficiency/initialization attribution study of an inherited unified representation, not a new architecture or novelty claim.

Full16 CPU reference is random scratch state only. Both native and coupled modes use the same reference construction overhead and preserve its ending CPU RNG stream; no inherited trained weights.
study.proposed_difference: Extend only two width guards and their errors to include item15; submit item15/action16/context16 with source-copy initialization as candidate.py, equal-capacity native15 and native14 controls, and a coupled full16 control for current numerical compatibility/timing. Each module is standalone. The existing coupled14 trial supplies the fourth factorial cell for width14/15 x native/coupled; do not rerun it as an independent seed. Predicted persistent width15 counts, derived by linear tensor-shape interpolation from measured width14/full16: total30,536,464, embeddings30,276,907, dense259,557 (4.7535% total reduction). Width14 counts29,012,475/28,760,598/251,877. These are predictions pending host measurement, not new measured results.
predictions: Full16 control reproduces source parameter/state/buffer/output and ending CPU RNG at the same incoming state; its host validation click AUC should reproduce0.660646940486458 if training is deterministic. Parity gates precede training of dependent cells; mismatch is implementation failure.

Width15 will reduce persistent parameters by1,523,989 versus full16; width14 by3,047,978. Native/coupled modes at each width must have identical registered shapes/counts and inference operators. No temporary reference remains registered.

Prospective pragmatic screen for NEW runs: click AUC delta to full16 >=-0.0003, click Logloss increase <=0.0001, >=4% fewer total parameters, and >=5% reduction in BOTH measured model-only batch p50 and p95 at the frozen batch, with no worse end-to-end validation inference time. This margin is selected after historical observations as a search decision, not a prespecified confirmation of width14 and not proof of exact AUC preservation. Always report signed deltas, including a loss within the margin. Strict preservation separately means observed delta>=0.

If both initialization modes at a width satisfy quality screen, reduction has local support beyond copied coordinates at the one host seed. If only coupling satisfies it, the supported object is the combined width/initialization recipe, not redundant capacity independently of initialization. Width x initialization interaction is [AUC(c15)-AUC(n15)]-[AUC(c14)-AUC(n14)], using original g1-r0016-coupled_item14_action16 for c14. Do not fit a monotonic law to widths8/12/14/15/16.

Report full-population all-four-task AUC/Logloss and auxiliary mean separately from click selection. Source auxiliary AUCs0.66415/0.70960/0.66880 are much below DIN0.84907/0.86490/0.87018; source click advantage is not a general multitask improvement. Retaining source quality never implies retaining DIN auxiliary quality.
falsifiers: Full16 compatibility, CPU RNG/data-order, source-coordinate copying, actual widths/aliases/padding, finite loss/backward, masking or gradient-route gate fails: stop dependent jobs and record an implementation failure with charged costs, not scientific counterevidence.

Both width15 initialization modes materially miss the declared click screen, or repeated matched source/candidate assessments show loss beyond margin: reject local near-source retention in this tested range. A single failed width15 initialization does not refute all capacity reductions.

Parameter savings occur but p50/p95 or end-to-end inference does not improve under matched host measurements: reject measured-speed benefit for that candidate; retain separate storage/quality observation.

Only source-coupled14 is favorable and native14/native15/coupled15 fail, or gains disappear across authorized paired seeds: classify the apparent width14 result as initialization/shape/selection sensitive, not robust redundant capacity.
Candidate improves click at the expense of auxiliary tasks or a history slice: retain exact tradeoff and counts; do not label the result uniform multitask improvement.
alternative_explanations: Shape-dependent assignment of random draws and initialization variance, rather than the amount of retained predictive information. Earlier item8 native/coupled AUC0.6513506160/0.6599120831 illustrates sensitivity, while item12 coupling was slightly worse than native.

BF16 kernel alignment, GPU scheduling/load and fixed overhead explain latency nonmonotonicity: width12 p50~11.61ms while width14~9.13ms. Parameter reduction alone predicts neither latency nor throughput.

One-epoch optimizer dynamics, input fan-in variance and Dice batch statistics change with omitted coordinates; source copying does not isolate asymptotic capacity or establish a biological/mechanistic redundancy claim.

Validation selection over many trajectories, one seed/data order and highly correlated repeated exposures can produce apparently favorable near-source doses. Endpoint replays reproduce one initialization, not independent evidence.

Inherited offline history/auxiliary label semantics and whole-window vocabularies restrict production transfer. Current history feedback may not be mature online; no real-time causal availability claim.

Across prior branches: halving all embeddings (g1-r0006-embedding_half, AUC0.65778185), halving dense widths (g1-r0006-dense_half,0.65947329), learned table8-to16 expansion (g1-r0007-table8_interact16,0.65878046), context8/item16 reallocation (g1-r0011-context8_item16,0.66009427), and attribute-only reduction (g1-r0013-id16_attr8,0.65965930) did not reproduce source click AUC. These are successful executions with unfavorable scientific outcomes, not runtime failures. They use differing operators/initializations and are not clean controls for the present native width dose. No earlier runtime error is pending.

Future intervals require host-available paired user-cluster predictions (not exposed to candidate); use no sample-independent significance assumption. If clustering/seed interface absent, report unavailable, not fabricated. No useful admissible experiment or integrity failure ends this branch.
